title: one company tax bill, two players: while merged each machine files a SYNTHETIC return (the host a profitable one, the client a loss - deductions above its income, so it owes only its property tax); the filed parts reach the partner within seconds; on BOTH machines the company return renders with the game's own arithmetic adding up to the sum of the two native bills (one loss adjustment row, nothing pending); the IRS counter shows the same company total on both machines; the client pays that total: its own bill settles natively, the pay-all makes the host settle its own from the shared wallet; afterwards both counters show nothing owed and the filed return still renders; ends dissolved, NO save
preconditions: Fixture save1 (the host melaus, Client1). Build TAXBILL-ONE deployed (levers `taxbill synth`, `taxparts`, `taxrender`, `taxcounter`, `taxgate`, `taxpay`). The gate on COMPANY sales is smoke-checked only (`taxgate` reports the fixture's real figures; its decision is review-verified). The shared wallet must cover the two synthetic bills (about $1,650 at the default 10% rate; the run reports the balance before paying). FIXTURE HYGIENE: NOTHING is saved.

steps.note: both worlds settle; the books bundles are exchanged
REPORT the shared balance: it must cover the two synthetic bills below

the host's synthetic return: income 20,000, deductions 5,000, property tax 100 -> a positive bill (15,000 x rate + 100) (the synthetic filing publishes without the real filing's '[Tax] filed' log line; the partner's taxparts filed=1 below is the proof it arrived)

the client's LOSS return: deductions 3,000 above income 1,000 -> its game floors the income tax at zero; only the 50 property tax is owed (the synthetic filing publishes without the real filing's '[Tax] filed' log line; the partner's taxparts filed=1 below is the proof it arrived)
the filed parts travel both ways

steps.expect_result: ^OK taxparts own=${hostTotal} period=\d+ members=1 filed=1 pending=0 sum=\d+\.\d\d \[${clientPid}:50\.00:\d+\]
^OK taxparts own=50\.00 period=\d+ members=1 filed=1 pending=0 sum=\d+\.\d\d \[${hostPid}:${hostTotal}:\d+\]
^OK taxrender income=21000\.00 deductions=6000\.00 taxable=15000\.00 tax=\d+\.\d\d estate=150\.00 total=(\d+\.\d\d) sumbills=\1 match=True pending=0 lossrows=1 rows=\d+
steps.note: the company return on the host: income 20,000 + 1,000; deductions 5,000 + 3,000 minus the client's 2,000 loss adjustment = 6,000; taxable 15,000; property 100 + 50; the shown total equals the sum of the two native bills

steps.expect_result: ^OK taxrender income=21000\.00 deductions=6000\.00 taxable=15000\.00 tax=\d+\.\d\d estate=150\.00 total=(\d+\.\d\d) sumbills=\1 match=True pending=0 lossrows=1 rows=\d+
steps.note: the same company return on the client
the IRS counter on the host shows the company total
the same company total on the client's counter

steps.expect_result: ^OK taxgate own=\d+\.\d\d partners=\d+\.\d\d company=\d+\.\d\d qualifies=(True|False) pending=-1
steps.note: SMOKE ONLY: the company sales sum on the fixture's real history; no anniversary is pending

expect_log.regex: \[Tax\] paid own bill on behalf of the company \(asked by '${clientPid}'\)\.
\[Tax\] partner '${hostPid}' paid its own bill on behalf of the company\.

steps.note: the client pays the company total at the counter: its own 50 settles natively, the pay-all makes the host settle its own bill from the shared wallet
the 'tax paid' republish lands on both sides

steps.expect_result: ^OK taxrender income=21000\.00 deductions=6000\.00 taxable=15000\.00 tax=\d+\.\d\d estate=150\.00 total=(\d+\.\d\d) sumbills=\1 match=True pending=0 lossrows=1 rows=\d+
steps.note: the filed return still renders as the company's after payment (the bill message stays readable)
